evidence.title: Gruta da Oliveira (Almonda Karst, Portugal): 100–45 ka Neanderthal remains
evidence.dateBasis: U-series, TL, OSL & radiocarbon stratigraphy
evidence.summary: Phalanges, metacarpals, cranial fragments, and teeth (Oliveira 1–10) from structured hearths in Zilhão's Almonda karst sequence near Torres Novas.
evidence.limits: Fragmentary postcranial/dental elements span Mousterian Layers 8–22.

evidence.title: Gruta Nova da Columbeira (Bombarral, Portugal): late western Neanderthal tooth
evidence.dateBasis: ESR & U-series of Mousterian breccias
evidence.summary: Human molar and Mousterian levels from the Portuguese Estremadura karst near the Atlantic coast.
evidence.limits: Early excavation stratigraphy; radiocarbon limits historically debated.

evidence.title: Gruta de Salemas (Loures, Lisbon, Portugal): late Neanderthal premolar
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified Mousterian lithic context
evidence.summary: Diagnostic deciduous/premolar dental evidence from coastal Lisbon karst caves documenting westernmost Eurasian Neanderthals.
evidence.limits: Small single-site dental record from mid-20th-century excavations.

evidence.title: Forbes' Quarry (Gibraltar): 1848 adult female cranium (Gibraltar 1) & aDNA
evidence.dateBasis: Morphology, breccia context & Bokelmann et al. (2019) endogenous aDNA
evidence.summary: Discovered in 1848 eight years before Feldhofer (recognized later), Gibraltar 1 is the first adult Neanderthal skull ever found; 2019 PNAS genome sequencing confirmed maternal female identity and Western European late Neanderthal affinities.
evidence.limits: Uncertain exact 19th-century breccia horizon without direct radiocarbon collagen.

evidence.title: Devil's Tower Rockshelter (Gibraltar 2): ~50–45 ka child cranium & aDNA
evidence.dateBasis: Garrod 1926 Mousterian travertine & 2019 PNAS genomic confirmation
evidence.summary: Five-year-old Neanderthal child cranium/mandible (Gibraltar 2) excavated by Dorothy Garrod alongside Mousterian hearths and marine shells, sequenced genetically alongside Forbes' Quarry in 2019.
evidence.limits: Radiocarbon on travertine matrix carries broad uncertainty.

evidence.title: Cova del Bolomor (Tavernes de la Valldigna, Valencia, Spain): 350–100 ka MIS 9–5e fossils
evidence.dateBasis: TL, OSL, ESR/U-series across 17 stratigraphic levels
evidence.summary: Isolated parietals, teeth, and fibula spanning MIS 9 to MIS 5e alongside Europe's clearest early hearths and tortoise/small-game processing.
evidence.limits: Small fragmentary hominin fossils span multiple interglacial cycles.

evidence.title: Pinilla del Valle / Calvero de la Higuera (Madrid, Spain): ~90–42 ka
evidence.dateBasis: TL, OSL & U-series across Camino, Buena Pinta & Navalmaíllo caves
evidence.summary: Neanderthal molars (Camino & Buena Pinta caves) plus Des-Cubierta child burial-linked symbolic horned skulls accumulation in Guadarrama highlands.
evidence.limits: Carnivore modification mixed some hyena-den assemblages at Camino.

evidence.title: Banyoles Travertine Quarry (Girona, Spain): ~65–45 ka disputed mandible
evidence.dateBasis: ESR & U-series travertine block dating (Grün 2006 / Keeling 2023)
evidence.summary: Virtually complete mandible recovered in 1887; 2023 JHE morphological reassessment shows unexpected lack of several derived Neanderthal chin/retromolar hallmarks despite U-series MIS 4–3 age.
evidence.limits: Quarry find lacks stone-tool association and sparks mosaic/Sapiens-introgression debate.

evidence.title: Cova del Gegant (Sitges, Barcelona, Spain): 60–49 ka mandibles & humerus
evidence.dateBasis: U-series, OSL & Bayesian 14C age model (Daura et al. 2021)
evidence.summary: Coastal Catalan sea cave preserving Gegant-1 mandible, humeri, and teeth bracketed between ~60 and ~49 ka along the Mediterranean coastal corridor.
evidence.limits: Waves periodically flooded outer cave galleries during sea-level highstands.

evidence.title: Cova Simanya (Sant Llorenç del Munt, Catalonia, Spain): >49 ka 54-bone assemblage
evidence.dateBasis: Morales et al. (2023) Frontiers bioarchaeology & stratigraphy
evidence.summary: Fifty-four newly recognized Neanderthal skeletal and dental elements from at least three individuals (adult, adolescent, child) excavated in NE Iberia.
evidence.limits: Historical 1978 excavation recovery limited direct bone collagen 14C preservation.

evidence.title: Cova del Salt & Cova Negra Hinterland / Alicante (Spain): 60–44 ka fossils
evidence.dateBasis: TL, OSL & micro-stratigraphic Mousterian dates
evidence.summary: El Salt (Alcoy) preserves six late Neanderthal adult teeth (Lezetxiki/Salt series) alongside lipid-preserved plant-rich Neanderthal coprolites and hearths.
evidence.limits: Dental wear limits population size estimation to small family groups.

evidence.title: Sima de las Palomas del Cabezo Gordo (Murcia, SE Spain): >100 bones & articulated burials
evidence.dateBasis: OSL, U-series & radiocarbon (~43–40 ka, Walker et al. 2008–2011; Zilhão 2017)
evidence.summary: One of the largest late Neanderthal skeletal samples anywhere (>100 craniodental & postcranial specimens of ~9 individuals, including Palomas 92/96–97 flexed burials sealed under stones).
evidence.limits: Heavy karst cementation requires micro-preparation; fine dating boundary sits around ~43–40 ka.

evidence.title: Boquete de Zafarraya (Alcaucín, Málaga, Spain): >46 ka mandible & femora
evidence.dateBasis: Revised ultrafiltered 14C (Wood 2013) & U-series/ESR (Kehl 2013)
evidence.summary: Classic adult mandible (Zafarraya 2) and femora showing strong Neanderthal traits and cutmarks; 2013 redating revised disputed ~32 ka claims back older than ~46 ka cal BP.
evidence.limits: Early conventional 14C dates (<35 ka) turned out to reflect unremoved modern consolidant contamination.

evidence.title: Cueva de la Carihuela (Piñar, Granada, Spain): ~80–42 ka parietals & teeth
evidence.dateBasis: TL, pollen & radiocarbon stratigraphy across Units VIII–V
evidence.summary: High-elevation Granada cave preserving juvenile frontal, adult parietals, and teeth across deep Mousterian sequences.
evidence.limits: Historical multi-phase excavations cause ongoing revision of uppermost Unit IV transition dates.

evidence.title: Lezetxiki Cave (Arrasate, Gipuzkoa, Spain): MIS 5/4 humerus & Neanderthal teeth
evidence.dateBasis: U-series, ESR & 2023 AJPA micro-CT dental reassessment (López-Onaindia)
evidence.summary: Adult female humerus (1964) and molar/premolar teeth along the Atlantic Cantabrian corridor showing strong classic Neanderthal internal enamel morphology.
evidence.limits: Complex breccia stratigraphy separated humerus (~MIS 6/5) from upper Mousterian teeth.

evidence.title: Axlor & Arrillor Caves (Basque Country, Spain): 50–42 ka Mousterian children teeth
evidence.dateBasis: Ultrafiltration 14C & micro-CT dental morphology
evidence.summary: Deciduous/permanent Neanderthal teeth associated with Quina and Levallois flake sequences bridging Cantabria and Aquitaine.
evidence.limits: Isolated shed or juvenile teeth only.

evidence.title: Cueva de Valdegoba (Huérmeces, Burgos, Spain): ~73 ka Neanderthal maxilla & phalanges
evidence.dateBasis: ESR & biochronological chamois-hunting assemblage
evidence.summary: Juvenile/adult Neanderthal maxilla fragment (VB 1) and postcrania in specialized northern Meseta alpine canyon hunting station.
evidence.limits: Limited radiometric collagen preserved in deeper layers.

evidence.title: El Castillo Cave Level 18/20 (Puente Viesgo, Spain): ~65–45 ka Mousterian fossils
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, U-series & Garralda et al. (2023) morphometrics
evidence.summary: Beneath Aurignacian and famous red-disk art walls, basal Mousterian layers at El Castillo yielded three Neanderthal juvenile/adult fossils examined by Garralda et al. (2023).
evidence.limits: 1910s Obermaier excavation recovery without modern spatial coordinates.

evidence.title: El Sidrón Cave (Borines, Asturias, Spain): ~49 ka 13-individual kinship & genome
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, OSL & amino-acid racemization (~49 ka)
evidence.summary: More than 2,500 exquisitely preserved bones of 13 related Neanderthals (3 men, 3 adolescent boys, 4 women, 3 infants) revealing patrilocal kin groups, chamomile/poplar dental calculus self-medication, and cannibalism.
evidence.limits: Secondary karst collapse flushed the group rapidly into Gallery III.

evidence.title: La Chapelle-aux-Saints (Corrèze, France): ~56–47 ka intentional adult burial
evidence.dateBasis: ESR tooth dating & Rendu et al. (2014) PNAS taphonomic re-excavation
evidence.summary: Iconic 1908 virtually complete skeleton of an elderly arthritic, nearly toothless adult male Neanderthal ('Old Man') deliberately placed inside an excavated rectangular pit with unmodified cave floor edges.
evidence.limits: Pathologies early skewed popular reconstructions toward an incorrect stooped stereotype; 2014 re-excavation vindicated intentional burial.

evidence.title: La Ferrassie (Savignac-de-Miremont, Dordogne, France): ~54–41 ka 8 Neanderthal burials
evidence.dateBasis: OSL & ultrafiltration 14C (LF1–LF8 ~54–41 ka, Balzeau 2020; Gómez-Olivencia 2018)
evidence.summary: Premier Neanderthal family cemetery: 8 individuals (two adults, six children/neonates, incl. LF1 complete adult male skeleton & LF8 child buried at ~41.7 ka) revealing sexual dimorphism, flexed pits, and pit stratigraphy.
evidence.limits: Early 1909–1921 trenching lacked fine sediment geochemistry until Balzeau's 2010–2020 re-excavations.

evidence.title: Le Moustier Rockshelter (Peyzac-le-Moustier, France): ~56–40 ka Mousterian type burials
evidence.dateBasis: TL & OSL (~56 ka Lower Shelter / ~41 ka LM1)
evidence.summary: Nameplate site of the Mousterian culture preserving Le Moustier 1 (adolescent male skeleton, 1908) and Le Moustier 2 (neonate skeleton rediscovered in museum boxes in 1996).
evidence.limits: WWII bombing in Berlin severely damaged Le Moustier 1 cranium; postcrania remain preserved.

evidence.title: Regourdou (Montignac-sur-Vézère, Dordogne, France): ~70 ka skeleton beside brown bear pit
evidence.dateBasis: MIS 4/5a biostratigraphy & Pablos/Gómez-Olivencia (2013–2019)
evidence.summary: Partial adult skeleton (Regourdou 1 mandible, arms, axial spine, feet) intentionally placed beneath a limestone slab cairn next to a stone-lined chamber holding brown bear bones—adjacent to Lascaux Hill.
evidence.limits: Whether bear pit and Neanderthal burial were strictly ritual-linked remains debated.

evidence.title: Roc de Marsal (Campagne-du-Bugue, Dordogne, France): ~65–50 ka child skeleton
evidence.dateBasis: TL & OSL (~65–50 ka) & Sandgathe et al. (2011) reassessment
evidence.summary: Exceptionally complete 2–4-year-old Neanderthal child skeleton discovered in 1961 within an asymmetric karst depression; 2011 reassessment questioned deliberate grave-digging vs natural pit preservation.
evidence.limits: Highlights thin line between intentional pit interment and rapid sediment covering.

evidence.title: Pech de l'Azé I (Carsac-Aillac, France): ~51–41 ka MTA Neanderthal child cranium
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, U-series & Jacobs et al. (2016) single-grain OSL
evidence.summary: Well-preserved ~2-year-old Neanderthal child skull and mandible from Layer 4 Mousterian of Acheulean Tradition (MTA Type B), directly anchored by ESR and OSL.
evidence.limits: Lacks associated postcrania; adjacent Pech IV records rich fire/manganese pigment use.

evidence.title: Combe-Grenal (Domme, Dordogne, France): 150–45 ka reference Mousterian & mandible
evidence.dateBasis: TL, ESR & François Bordes master sequence (Levels 1–65)
evidence.summary: Over 65 stratified Mousterian horizons preserving classic Neanderthal teeth, mandibular fragments, and cutmarked bone documenting climate-driven shifts between Quina, Ferrassie, and Denticulate technologies.
evidence.limits: Sparse hominin bone count relative to vast lithic/faunal recovery.

evidence.title: La Roche à Pierrot (Saint-Césaire, Charente-Maritime, France): ~42 ka 'Pierrette'
evidence.dateBasis: TL & ultrafiltration direct collagen 14C (42–40 ka cal BP)
evidence.summary: Crushed partial adult skeleton ('Pierrette') excavated in 1979 from Châtelperronian levels, demonstrating Neanderthals persisted alongside or immediately after the arrival of Aurignacian technologies in SW France; skull shows healed weapon blow.
evidence.limits: Minor stratigraphic mixing debate between underlying Denticulate Mousterian and Châtelperronian units.

evidence.title: La Quina (Gardes-le-Pontaroux, Charente, France): ~65–43 ka >20 individuals (H5/H18)
evidence.dateBasis: TL, ESR & Henri-Martin / Jelinek-Debénath excavations
evidence.summary: Classic Quina Mousterian type locality yielding H5 complete adult female skeleton/cranium, H18 remarkably intact 8-year-old child cranium, and bone retouchers.
evidence.limits: 1908–1920s collections span Quina and Denticulate levels across ~20 kyr.

evidence.title: Les Pradelles (Marillac-le-Franc, Charente, France): ~57 ka Quina reindeer-camp & cannibalism
evidence.dateBasis: TL, OSL & Mussini et al. (2011) C. R. Palevol
evidence.summary: High-altitude/karst chimney Quina reindeer butchery factory containing >100 cut-marked and intentionally fractured Neanderthal bones & bone retouchers evidencing nutritional cannibalism.
evidence.limits: Skeletal fragments commingled with heavily processed reindeer carcasses.

evidence.title: Chez-Pinaud Jonzac (Charente-Maritime, France): ~50–40 ka Quina bonebed & teeth
evidence.dateBasis: TL, ESR & Rendu et al. (2023) Frontiers bioarchaeology
evidence.summary: Isolated Neanderthal teeth and postcrania embedded within monumental seasonal reindeer-slaughter bonebeds and Quina scraper workshops.
evidence.limits: Sparse hominin fossils amid dense faunal accumulations.

evidence.title: La Chaise-de-Vouthon (Suard & Bourgeois-Delaunay, Charente, France): 185–110 ka
evidence.dateBasis: U-series speleothems (MIS 6 Abri Suard / MIS 5e Bourgeois-Delaunay) & Zanolli 2020
evidence.summary: Dual adjoining caves preserving 50+ pre-Würm early Neanderthal remains: Suard (MIS 6 ~185–128 ka parietal/teeth) and Bourgeois-Delaunay (MIS 5e ~128–110 ka BD 1 mandible, cranial vault, femur).
evidence.limits: Early vs classic Neanderthal mosaic anatomy tracks MIS 6 to MIS 5e transitions.

evidence.title: Fontéchevade (Montbron, Charente, France): ~150–40 ka parietal/frontal fossils
evidence.dateBasis: Chase et al. (2009) ESR/OSL & radiocarbon revision
evidence.summary: Historically misinterpreted in 1947 as evidence of an ancient 'pre-sapiens' vault without browridges (Fontéchevade II); modern micro-CT/redating confirmed classic Neanderthal affinities (Fontéchevade I small-fragment frontal + Tayacian/Mousterian MIS 6–3 context).
evidence.limits: Mixed cave-roof breccias complicated 1947 age assignment.

evidence.title: La Niche at Montmaurin (Haute-Garonne, France): ~240–190 ka archaic/early Neanderthal mandible
evidence.dateBasis: U-series, biostratigraphy & Vialet et al. (2018) PLOS ONE
evidence.summary: Complete adult mandible (Montmaurin-La Niche, MIS 7 ~200–240 ka) with archaic-to-Neanderthal mosaic symphysis and incipient retromolar space bridging Middle Pleistocene lineages into Neanderthals.
evidence.limits: Vertical chimney breccia lacked direct radiometric ash.

evidence.title: Angles-sur-l'Anglin & Rochelot (Vienne/Charente, France): 60–42 ka
evidence.dateBasis: Biochronology & late Mousterian stratigraphy
evidence.summary: Neanderthal teeth and cranial fragments from northern Aquitaine / Loire threshold corridors linking Dordogne and Paris Basin.
evidence.limits: Small isolated samples in museum archives.

evidence.title: Tourville-la-Rivière (Seine-Maritime, Normandy, France): ~200 ka early Neanderthal arm
evidence.dateBasis: ESR & U-series fluvial terrace dating (~226–183 ka, Faivre et al. 2014)
evidence.summary: Left humerus, ulna, and radius of a young adult (~200 ka MIS 7) beside butchered horse/aurochs carcasses in Seine meander gravels, bearing healed repetitive spear-throwing microtrauma.
evidence.limits: Isolated left forelimb without cranium.

evidence.title: Biache-Saint-Vaast (Pas-de-Calais, Northern France): ~230–180 ka early Neanderthals
evidence.dateBasis: TL, ESR & Martín-Francés et al. (2022)
evidence.summary: Two partial skulls (BSV 1 young female, BSV 2 older individual) excavated cleanly from alluvial silt with Levallois points showing unmistakable Neanderthal occipital bunning and inner-ear labyrinth at MIS 7.
evidence.limits: Partial crania without mandibles.

evidence.title: Grotte Mandrin (Malataverne, Rhône Valley, France): ~50–42 ka 'Thorin' isolated lineage
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian 14C, OSL & Slimak/Fuchs/Sikora (2022–2024)
evidence.summary: Partial cranium, maxilla, and 31 teeth of adult male 'Thorin' stratified above the ephemeral ~54 ka H. sapiens Neronian excursion; 2024 Cell Genomics DNA revealed a deeply divergent Mediterranean Neanderthal lineage isolated from classic European peers for ~50,000 years!
evidence.limits: Single genome revolutionizes extinction models by proving fractured small local populations lacked inter-group gene flow.

evidence.title: Baume Moula-Guercy (Soyons, Ardèche, France): ~120 ka MIS 5e cannibalized kin
evidence.dateBasis: TL, paleosol MIS 5e & Richards et al. (2021–2024) cranial/mandibular studies
evidence.summary: Minimum 6 individuals (>120 bones of adults, adolescents, children) defleshed, disarticulated, and marrow-cracked in Layer XV during Last Interglacial temperate woodland maxima.
evidence.limits: Endocannibalism vs dietary stress during rapid woodland biome change remains debated.

evidence.title: Payre (Rompon, Ardèche, France): 250–125 ka MIS 8–5e fossils & fish/bird diet
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, U-series & Hardy/Moncel (2011, 2020)
evidence.summary: Collapsed limestone terrace shelter yielding human teeth and Payre 15 mandible alongside early Levallois/discoid cores with fish scales, avian bones, and starchy plants.
evidence.limits: Early Middle Paleolithic transition specimens.

evidence.title: Bau de l'Aubesier (Vaucluse, Provence, France): 190–100 ka Aubesier 11 pathology
evidence.dateBasis: TL burnt-flint dating (~190–140 ka) & Lebel/Trinkaus (2001 PNAS)
evidence.summary: Twelve human teeth and the famous Aubesier 11 adult mandible preserving extreme antemortem tooth loss and alveolar resorption proving compassionate caregiving for disabled elders nearly 200 ka ago.
evidence.limits: Mandibular fragments derived from complex Mont Ventoux rockfall deposits.

evidence.title: Grotte du Lazaret (Nice, Maritime Alps, France): 190–130 ka MIS 6 coastal camp
evidence.dateBasis: ESR/U-series & marine-terrace stratigraphy
evidence.summary: Over 25 late MIS 6 early Neanderthal cranial fragments, parietals, and teeth found within organized seaweed-bedding habitation floors facing glacial Mediterranean shores.
evidence.limits: Pre-Eemian early Neanderthal features complement Suard and Ehringsdorf.

evidence.title: Grotte de l'Hortus (Valflaunès, Hérault, France): ~50–40 ka >20 individuals
evidence.dateBasis: Würm II cold-phase fauna & Williams et al. (2019)
evidence.summary: Remains of ~20–36 Neanderthals (adults and children) deposited alongside mountain-ibex hunting camps near Pic Saint-Loup.
evidence.limits: Cold-steppe open karst stratigraphy; some researchers argue episodic cannibalism.

evidence.title: Châteauneuf-sur-Charente & Petit-Puymoyen (Charente, France): 65–45 ka child & adult teeth
evidence.dateBasis: Classic Charente Mousterian child skull & mandible fossils
evidence.summary: Châteauneuf-sur-Charente (2-year-old Neanderthal child) and Petit-Puymoyen jaw/teeth bridging Quina and Fontéchevade along the Charente karst corridor.
evidence.limits: Historical early 20th-century excavations.

evidence.title: Grottes de l'Hyène & du Bison at Arcy-sur-Cure (Yonne, France): 55–42 ka Mousterian fossils
evidence.dateBasis: Leroi-Gourhan Mousterian & early Châtelperronian levels below Grotte du Renne
evidence.summary: Directly adjoining Grotte du Renne along the Cure River cliffs, Grotte de l'Hyène and Grotte du Bison yielded classic Mousterian Neanderthal mandibles and teeth preceding the final ~42 ka transition.
evidence.limits: Legacy Cure-bank stratigraphy.

evidence.title: Grotte du Portel-Ouest (Ariège), Crouzade (Aude) & Vergisson (France): 60–40 ka
evidence.dateBasis: Mousterian teeth & maxillae across Pyrenean/Burgundian corridors
evidence.summary: Complementary late Mousterian Neanderthal teeth and child mandibles at Portel-Ouest, La Crouzade, and Vergisson showing dense regional continuity prior to ~40 ka.
evidence.limits: Small dental collections spanning multi-site French regional inventories.

evidence.title: La Cotte de St Brelade (Jersey, Channel Islands): 240–48 ka mammoths & late teeth
evidence.dateBasis: OSL, TL & Compton et al. (2021) JHE dental morphology
evidence.summary: Dramatic granite sea-ravine ambush site preserving mammoth/woolly-rhino stampede cliffs (~240–130 ka) and 13 permanent teeth (1910/1911) recently re-analyzed in 2021 as <48 ka late Neanderthal/admixed population morphology!
evidence.limits: Pre-war 1910–11 trenching separated teeth slightly from later mammoth bonebed levels.

evidence.title: Zeeland Ridges / North Sea ('Krijn', Doggerland, Netherlands): >45 ka submerged Neanderthal
evidence.dateBasis: Morphology & stable nitrogen/carbon isotopes (Hublin et al. 2009 JHE)
evidence.summary: Supraorbital frontal fragment of a young adult male nicknamed 'Krijn', dredged from the North Sea floor ~15 km off Zeeland—preserving a benign intradiploic epidermoid cyst above his right brow and high meat-eating 15N isotopes.
evidence.limits: Dredged offshore Doggerland sediment without direct collagen 14C date.

evidence.title: Engis Cave ('Engis 2', Awirs, Liège, Belgium): 1829 FIRST Neanderthal child skull ever found
evidence.dateBasis: Schmerling (1833) / Devièse et al. (2021 PNAS) CSRA ~44–40.6 ka
evidence.summary: Excavated by Philippe-Charles Schmerling in 1829—nearly 30 years BEFORE Feldhofer! Engis 2 (~4–6-year-old Neanderthal child cranium) sat unrecognized alongside Pleistocene rhino bones until late 19th–20th c. reclassification; dated ~42 ka.
evidence.limits: Historically commingled with Neolithic Engis 1 burial until careful fluorine/14C work separated them.

evidence.title: Spy Cave (Betch aux Rotches, Namur, Belgium): ~43–40.6 ka Spy I & II skeletons
evidence.dateBasis: Devièse et al. (2021 PNAS) hydroxyproline single-amino-acid 14C
evidence.summary: Discovered in 1886, Spy I and Spy II proved scientifically that Neanderthals were truly fossil Pleistocene humans buried with cold-steppe fauna and Mousterian tools; 2021 compound-specific dating tightly pinned them at ~44.2–40.6 ka cal BP.
evidence.limits: Earlier bulk collagen 14C gave falsely young ~36 ka ages due to bovine museum glue contamination.

evidence.title: Goyet Troisième Caverne (Gesves, Namur, Belgium): ~45–40 ka cannibalism & bone tools
evidence.dateBasis: Direct collagen 14C & Rougier et al. (2016) Sci. Rep.
evidence.summary: Largest northern European late Neanderthal fossil cluster (~99 specimens from >=5 individuals), extensively cut-marked, fractured for marrow, and fashioned into four retouchers (bone tools made on Neanderthal femora/tibia!), yielding nuclear and mtDNA genomes.
evidence.limits: Ex-situ 1868 Dupont excavation boxes reassembled via ancient DNA & direct AMS 14C.

evidence.title: Scladina Cave (Sclayn, Andenne, Belgium): ~127 ka juvenile & nuclear DNA
evidence.dateBasis: Gamma spectrometry, TL & Peyrégne et al. (2019 Sci. Adv.) nuclear genome
evidence.summary: Right mandible, maxilla, and 16 teeth of an 8-year-old child (~127 ka Unit 4A) providing the oldest Belgian nuclear genome, linking early Western European Neanderthals to later 40 ka Belgian/Croatian lineages across 80,000 years!
evidence.limits: Disarticulated juvenile jaw fragments in flowstone/alluvial clay.

evidence.title: Trou de La Naulette (Dinant, Belgium) & Fonds-de-Forêt / Trou Walou: 50–40 ka
evidence.dateBasis: 1866 mandible discovery & Devièse (2021) Belgian synthesis
evidence.summary: Excavated in 1866 along the Lesse River, La Naulette's chinless mandible gave critical early anatomical proof of Neanderthal antiquity, alongside Fonds-de-Forêt's ~44 ka femur and Couvin/Walou molars.
evidence.limits: Fragmentary postcranial/dental items from classic 19th-century Belgian digs.

evidence.title: Kleine Feldhofer Grotte (Neander Valley, Düsseldorf, Germany): 1856 TYPE SITE (~42–40 ka)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS 14C & Schmitz et al. (2002 PNAS) 1997 cave-dump re-excavation
evidence.summary: The August 1856 quarry discovery ('Neanderthal 1', holotype of Homo neanderthalensis, named by William King 1864). Schmitz & Thissen (1997) dramatically relocated the destroyed cave's dumped sediment, matching new humerus/zygomatic fragments directly onto the 1856 bones and identifying two additional individuals (~42–40 ka).
evidence.limits: Quarrying destroyed the original limestone cliff in 1856; all context stems from sediment screening & direct 14C/aDNA.

evidence.title: Steinheim an der Murr (Baden-Württemberg, Germany): ~300–250 ka proto-Neanderthal skull
evidence.dateBasis: Holsteinian/MIS 9–7 terrace stratigraphy & Buzi et al. (2021) retrodeformation
evidence.summary: Remarkably complete crushed adult cranium (Steinheim 1, 1933) exhibiting incipient Neanderthal lambdoid/supraorbital traits alongside more globular midface anatomy—pivotal anchor for the accretion model.
evidence.limits: Post-depositional compression deformed left side of face prior to digital retrodeformation.

evidence.title: Ehringsdorf & Taubach (Weimar, Thuringia, Germany): 230–120 ka travertine fossils
evidence.dateBasis: U-series Lower Travertine ~230 ka (Blackwell & Schwarcz 1986) / MIS 5e Taubach
evidence.summary: Adult parietal/mandibles/crania from Ehringsdorf (~230 ka MIS 7 interglacial travertine) showing mixed archaic/derived Neanderthal anatomy plus cut/burnt trauma, paired with MIS 5e ~125 ka Taubach isolated molars.
evidence.limits: Commercial travertine quarrying disturbed exact micro-provenance between lower and upper travertines.

evidence.title: Hohlenstein-Stadel (Lone Valley, Swabian Jura, Germany): ~124 ka divergent femur mtDNA
evidence.dateBasis: Posth et al. (2017 Nature Comm.) molecular clock & Peyrégne (2019)
evidence.summary: Isolated 124 ka right femoral shaft ('HST') carrying an extraordinarily divergent mitochondrial haplotype splitting ~270 ka from other Neanderthals—implying an early African gene flow into Neanderthals before >200 ka—plus matching 120 ka Scladina/HST nuclear continuity.
evidence.limits: Only a carnivore-gnawed femur shaft preserved in basal Mousterian layer.

evidence.title: Salzgitter-Lebenstedt (Lower Saxony, Germany): ~58–48 ka reindeer-hunter skull & ZooMS
evidence.dateBasis: AMS 14C & Hublin et al. (2023 JQS) ZooMS/chronology
evidence.summary: Open-air Micoquian tundra ambush station yielding occipital/parietal skull fragments (1952), hundreds of barbed-point/bone tools, and mass reindeer slaughter near northern ice margins (~52°N).
evidence.limits: Cold wetland slump mixed two late MIS 4–3 levels.

evidence.title: Ochtendung & Sarstedt / Warendorf (Germany): 160–45 ka Rhineland & North Plain skulls
evidence.dateBasis: Eifel volcano caldera & NW German gravel pit cranial finds
evidence.summary: Crater-basin skullcap at Ochtendung (East Eifel) alongside Sarstedt and Warendorf cranial vaults anchoring western German plains between Feldhofer and Bavaria.
evidence.limits: Quarry/gravel-pit recovery contexts.

evidence.title: Reilingen (Upper Rhine Valley, Baden-Württemberg, Germany): ~200–130 ka early skull
evidence.dateBasis: Rhine alluvial terrace morphology (Buzi et al. 2021)
evidence.summary: Adult occipital, parietals, and right temporal recovered along Upper Rhine gravels displaying classic Neanderthal suprainiac fossa and incipient lambdoid flattening.
evidence.limits: Dredged terrace deposit.

evidence.title: Sesselfelsgrotte & Klausennische (Altmühl Valley, Bavaria, Germany): ~50–40 ka Micoquian fossils
evidence.dateBasis: Bavarian Micoquian stratigraphy & radiocarbon dating
evidence.summary: Fetal/neonatal/adult Neanderthal teeth and postcrania in Bavaria's upper Danube corridor linking Swabia/Rhineland and Moravian Kůlna/Šipka Micoquian sites.
evidence.limits: Fetal bone preservation limits craniometric scoring.

evidence.title: Grotte de Cotencher & Saint-Brais (Jura Mountains, Switzerland): ~65–45 ka alpine Neanderthals
evidence.dateBasis: Alpine karst Mousterian biostratigraphy & maxilla/incisor finds
evidence.summary: Highest confirmed Alpine cave Neanderthal maxilla (Cotencher, Neuchâtel) and St-Brais II incisor showing Neanderthal cold-season foraging across Jura passes.
evidence.limits: Sparse isolated elements near glaciated Alpine ice margins.

evidence.title: Altamura Man / Grotta di Lamalunga (Apulia, Italy): 172–130 ka complete encrusted skeleton
evidence.dateBasis: U-Th calcite coralloid dating & Profico et al. (2023 Commun. Biol.)
evidence.summary: The most complete early Neanderthal skeleton known globally, still fused by sparkling calcite 'cave popcorn' deep in an underground karst shaft at Altamura; 2015 extraction yielded oldest Neanderthal mtDNA and 2023 virtual endoscopy illuminated sinus/endocranial transition.
evidence.limits: Encrusted in situ under protected UNESCO-style karst rules; only small scapula fragment physically sampled.

evidence.title: Saccopastore 1 & 2 (Aniene River, Rome, Italy): ~250 ka MIS 7 earliest classic Neanderthals
evidence.dateBasis: Revised MIS 7 40Ar/39Ar fluvial terrace dating (Marra et al. 2015 QSR)
evidence.summary: Two exceptionally preserved crania (1929 female Saccopastore 1, 1935 male Saccopastore 2) recovered in Roman gravel quarries; 2015 revision pushed them back from MIS 5e to ~250 ka MIS 7, making them the oldest complete classic Neanderthal crania!
evidence.limits: Modern urban Rome now overlies the original Aniene gravel pit.

evidence.title: Grotta Breuil & Grotta del Fossellone (Monte Circeo, Latium, Italy): ~55–42 ka
evidence.dateBasis: ESR & Late Pontinian Mousterian sequences (Rubini & Zaio 2026)
evidence.summary: Neanderthal cranial parietal (Breuil 1) and child mandible/molars (Fossellone 3) supplementing neighboring Grotta Guattari along Italy's Pontinian coastline.
evidence.limits: Tiny shell-pebble Pontinian Mousterian industries reflect raw-material constraints.

evidence.title: Grotta di Fumane (Lessini Mountains, Verona, Italy): ~50–43 ka feather use & teeth
evidence.dateBasis: AMS 14C ultrafiltration & Richards/Peresani (2013, 2021)
evidence.summary: Neanderthal deciduous teeth beneath earliest Uluzzian, famous for cut-marked Alpine vulture/eagle wing feathers, ochered marine shell, and strontium-isotope mobility across northern Italy.
evidence.limits: Isolated shed deciduous teeth only.

evidence.title: Riparo Mezzena & Riparo Tagliente (Verona, Italy): ~55–40 ka Lessini jaws & burials
evidence.dateBasis: Condemi/Caramelli (2013 PLOS ONE) & Longo (2012 Quat. Int.)
evidence.summary: Mezzena adult mandible & cranial fragments (once debated for late interbreeding chin morphology, though recent collagen/14C shows complex chronology) alongside Tagliente Mousterian teeth and bone.
evidence.limits: 2013–2016 redating debates historical interbreeding interpretations on Mezzena jaw.

evidence.title: Grotta del Cavallo (Nardò, Apulia, Italy): >45 ka Mousterian child teeth beneath Uluzzian
evidence.dateBasis: 14C & tephra Campanian Ignimbrite (Benazzi et al. 2011 Nature)
evidence.summary: Lower Mousterian Layer F yielded true Neanderthal deciduous molars directly beneath Layer E Uluzzian teeth proven in 2011 to belong to >43 ka early Homo sapiens—anchoring Italy's replacement boundary.
evidence.limits: Earlier decades misattributed overlying Uluzzian teeth to Neanderthals until 2011 micro-CT.

evidence.title: Roccia San Sebastiano (Mondragone, Campania, Italy): 45–42 ka direct-dated teeth
evidence.dateBasis: Oxilia et al. (2022 AJPA) & ultrafiltration 14C
evidence.summary: Direct evidence that late Neanderthal occupation and deciduous molar morphology persisted immediately prior to Campania's Upper Paleolithic technological transition.
evidence.limits: Single-cave dental assemblage.

evidence.title: Grotta dei Santi (Monte Argentario, Tuscany) & Caverna delle Fate (Liguria, Italy): 75–42 ka
evidence.dateBasis: Italian Tyrrhenian Mousterian dental & juvenile mandible records
evidence.summary: Coastal Tuscan/Ligurian caves yielding Caverna delle Fate juvenile/adult jaws and teeth (~75–60 ka) plus Monte Argentario Mousterian foraging levels along exposed glacial Tyrrhenian shelves.
evidence.limits: Regional cave-by-cave dental records.

evidence.title: Archi (Calabria) & Grotta di Santa Croce (Bisceglie, Apulia, Italy): 80–40 ka southern Italy
evidence.dateBasis: Histology & southern Italian Neanderthal catalogue (Sci. Rep. 2021)
evidence.summary: Archi 1 child mandible (~45 ka near Strait of Messina) and Santa Croce adult femur (Apulia) documenting Neanderthals at the southernmost toe of mainland Italy.
evidence.limits: Dispersed southern coastal caves.

evidence.title: Kůlna Cave (Moravian Karst, Sloup, Czechia): ~50–45 ka Layer 7a Micoquian maxilla
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, 14C & Central European Micoquian sequence (Jöris & Neruda 2022)
evidence.summary: Right maxilla with teeth (Kůlna 1), parietal, and teeth stratified inside rich Micoquian (Keilmesser) Layer 7a inside Moravia's monumental karst tunnel.
evidence.limits: Direct aDNA recovery has remained limited compared to Polish/Croatian sites.

evidence.title: Šipka Cave & Švédův stůl / Ochoz (Moravia, Czechia): 1880 child jaw & adult mandible
evidence.dateBasis: Late Middle Paleolithic Moravian bioarchaeology (Jöris 2022)
evidence.summary: Šipka child mandible (1880—another critical 19th-century Neanderthal proof beside Spy!) and adult Ochoz / Švédův stůl mandible from Moravian river corridors linking Danube and Oder valleys.
evidence.limits: Historic 1880/1905 excavations lost micro-stratigraphic radiocarbon context.

evidence.title: Gánovce (Poprad) & Šaľa (Slovakia): 105–70 ka travertine brain endocast & frontal
evidence.dateBasis: U-series MIS 5e travertine & Eisová et al. (2019) paleoneurology
evidence.summary: Natural calcite mineral endocast preserving cortical convolutions inside MIS 5e–5d travertine at Gánovce (~105 ka) plus Šaľa 1 & 2 frontals/parietal dredged from Váh River gravels in western Slovakia.
evidence.limits: Travertine cast preserves external brain/meningeal anatomy without intact cranial bone table.

evidence.title: Stajnia Cave (Kraków-Częstochowa Upland, Poland): ~116–45 ka northernmost Carpathian aDNA
evidence.dateBasis: U-series, aDNA molecular clock & Picin et al. (2020 Sci. Rep.; 2026 Curr. Biol.)
evidence.summary: Three Neanderthal molars including S5000 (~116–82 ka) yielding the oldest central/eastern European Neanderthal mtDNA genome and showing multi-individual maternal turnover linking Poland with North Caucasus Mezmaiskaya!
evidence.limits: Isolated teeth excavated with Micoquian bifacial knives in periglacial cave silt.

evidence.title: Ciemna Cave (Ojców National Park, Poland): ~115 ka child tooth & digested phalanges
evidence.dateBasis: OSL & Willman et al. (2019 J. Paleol. Archaeol.)
evidence.summary: Neanderthal deciduous molar and two child manual phalanges bearing acid digestion pitting (probably passed through a giant bird's digestive tract—one of Europe's rarest taphonomic findings!).
evidence.limits: Isolated pediatric elements in MIS 5c–5a loessy sediments.

evidence.title: Subalyuk Cave (Bükk Mountains, Northern Hungary): ~40–38 ka direct-dated woman & child
evidence.dateBasis: Direct ultrafiltered 14C dating (Mester et al. 2023)
evidence.summary: Adult female sacrum/teeth and ~3-year-old child cranium/mandible (Subalyuk 1 & 2); 2023 direct radiocarbon dating confirms Subalyuk among the very youngest Neanderthals in the Carpathian Basin (~40 ka cal BP).
evidence.limits: Original 1932 excavation limited spatial plotting between late Mousterian sublayers.

evidence.title: Pešturina & Velika/Mala Balanica (Jelašnica Gorge, Serbia): 400–45 ka Balkan continuum
evidence.dateBasis: TL, ESR & Lindal (2020) / Radović (2025 AJPA)
evidence.summary: Mala Balanica (~400 ka BH-1 mandible lacking derived Neanderthal traits) and Velika Balanica (~300 ka) contrast with late Pleistocene Pešturina's true Neanderthal molar and bone bearing parallel symbolic incisions.
evidence.limits: Deeply fractured Balkan karst sequence spans Middle Pleistocene isolation vs Late Pleistocene Neanderthal gene flow.

evidence.title: Kalamakia & Lakonis Caves (Mani Peninsula, Greece): 100–40 ka southern Balkan coast
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, U-series, OSL & Panagopoulou (2002) / Harvati (2013)
evidence.summary: Fourteen Neanderthal teeth and cranial fragments from Kalamakia (~100–40 ka) plus a strontium-isotope mobile ~44–40 ka Neanderthal molar from Lakonis I, proving southern Greece served as a warm Mediterranean refugium.
evidence.limits: Submerged lower coastal karst shelves conceal additional Pleistocene shore camps.

evidence.title: Ohaba Ponor / Bordul Mare (Hunedoara, Romania): ~50–40 ka Transylvanian phalanges
evidence.dateBasis: Carpathian Mousterian stratigraphy (Dogandžić 2023)
evidence.summary: Diagnostic manual/pedal phalanges from Carpathian Transylvania just north of Peștera cu Oase, anchoring Neanderthal presence inside Romania prior to Oase 1 admixture.
evidence.limits: Small sample without direct collagen radiocarbon dating.

evidence.title: Kiik-Koba Grotto (Crimea): ~50–40 ka adult male & infant pit burials
evidence.dateBasis: AMS 14C & Crimean Micoquian stratigraphy
evidence.summary: Discovered 1924: deeply dug burial pit holding the lower limbs, hands, and teeth of an adult male (Kiik-Koba 1, showing unusually massive muscular attachments and hyperostosis) alongside a 1-year-old infant pit burial.
evidence.limits: Early excavation separated skull from postcrania before modern documentation.

evidence.title: Zaskalnaya V & VI (Ak-Kaya Cliff, Belogorsk, Crimea): 60–40 ka graves & engraved bird bone
evidence.dateBasis: AMS 14C & Majkić et al. (2017 PLOS ONE)
evidence.summary: Six Micoquian burials/individuals across Zaskalnaya VI (incl. triple child pit & mandibles) beside a raven radius notched with seven purposefully equidistant geometric grooves (Majkić 2017).
evidence.limits: Upper Layer II–III dates span the ~45–40 ka Crimean late refugium boundary.

evidence.title: Starosele (Bakhchisarai, Crimea): ~46–40 ka ZooMS/aDNA link to Altai Siberia (PNAS 2025)
evidence.dateBasis: Pigott et al. (2025 PNAS) ZooMS, direct 14C & mitogenome
evidence.summary: ZooMS peptide screening of unrecognized bone splinters uncovered a new ~46–45 ka late Neanderthal femoral shaft ('Starosele 3') whose mitochondrial genome falls close to Chagyrskaya/Okladnikov in Altai Siberia—proving a >3,000-km steppe highway across Eurasia!
evidence.limits: Distinguishes authentic ~45 ka Neanderthal femur from a historically intrusive Holocene child burial at Starosele.

evidence.title: Karabi Tamchin & Kabazi II (Crimean Mountains): 60–40 ka upland teeth
evidence.dateBasis: Crimean highlands Mousterian sequence
evidence.summary: High-plateau (730 m) Crimean hunting station yielding isolated Neanderthal molars inside Micoquian reindeer/wild-ass seasonal camps.
evidence.limits: Minimal skeletal material; complements Ak-Kaya and Bakhchisarai sites.

evidence.title: Rozhok I (Azov Coast) & Sukhaya Mechetka (Volga, Russia): 80–45 ka steppe frontier
evidence.dateBasis: Eemian/Early Valdai terrace & Volga loess stratigraphy
evidence.summary: Northern Black Sea / Azov permanent molar (Rozhok I, Micoquian Level IV) and nearby Volga open-air mammoth/bison camp Sukhaya Mechetka anchoring the Russian Plain corridor east toward Kazakhstan/Altai.
evidence.limits: Sukhaya Mechetka preserves hearths & Micoquian bifaces rather than intact bones; Rozhok contributes direct dental fossil evidence.

evidence.title: Mezmaiskaya Cave (Krasnodar, North Caucasus, Russia): ~70–42 ka Mezmaiskaya 1 & 2 genomes
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, Pinhasi et al. (2011 PNAS) & Andreeva et al. (2022 Sci. Rep.)
evidence.summary: Exquisitely preserved Layer 3 neonate burial (~70–60 ka Mezmaiskaya 1) and Layer 2 infant (~45–43 ka Mezmaiskaya 2), yielding foundational Caucasus nuclear/mtDNA genomes linking North Caucasus Micoquians to late Western Europe & Altai turnovers.
evidence.limits: Early ~29 ka claim refuted by 2011 ultrafiltered 14C (~40–43 ka extinction).

evidence.title: Barakaevskaya & Matuzka / Monasheskaya Caves (North Caucasus, Russia): 120–45 ka
evidence.dateBasis: Doronicheva et al. (2023 PLOS ONE) & Liubin Caucasus excavations
evidence.summary: Child mandible (Barakaevskaya), isolated molars (Monasheskaya, Matuzka) spanning Kuban highland Micoquian & Zagros-like facies across the northern slope of the Greater Caucasus.
evidence.limits: Fragmentary isolated child mandibles/teeth.

evidence.title: Ortvale Klde (Imereti, Western Georgia): 55–42 ka Levantine-Zagros Mousterian molar
evidence.dateBasis: Cullen et al. (2021 JHE) tephra/AMS & Doronicheva 2023
evidence.summary: Adult/child Neanderthal teeth from Layer 5 in the Southern Caucasus Rioni-Kvirila karst, sharply separated culturally from North Caucasus Micoquians until Upper Paleolithic turnover.
evidence.limits: Single-basin teeth plus rich Levallois-Mousterian obsidian transport.

evidence.title: Sakajia, Djruchula, Bronze & Bondi Caves (Georgia) & Azokh (Armenia/Caucasus): 200–40 ka
evidence.dateBasis: TL, ESR & Pleurdeau/Tushabramishvili (2012 JHE)
evidence.summary: Dense Georgian Southern Caucasus cluster: Sakajia maxilla/teeth, Djruchula early elongated-blade Mousterian molar (~140–200 ka), Bronze Cave child tooth, Bondi Cave tooth/obsidian, and Lesser Caucasus Azokh mandible.
evidence.limits: Small dental collections spanning broad Middle-to-Upper Pleistocene phases.

evidence.title: Karain Cave E (Antalya, SW Turkey): ~120–60 ka Anatolian Neanderthal teeth & tibia
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, U-series & Mediterranean Anatolia excavations
evidence.summary: Multi-chamber Taurus foothills karst site preserving Neanderthal teeth and postcranial shafts inside thick Zagros/Levantine-style Mousterian travertines bridging the Levant and Balkans.
evidence.limits: Older early excavations partially mixed transitional upper boundaries.

evidence.title: Kebara Cave (Mount Carmel, Israel): ~60–50 ka 'Moshe' (KMH2) skeleton & hyoid bone
evidence.dateBasis: TL & ESR (Bar-Yosef, Vandermeersch et al. 1992 Curr. Anthropol.)
evidence.summary: Iconic KMH2 adult male burial preserving complete ribcage, spine, pelvis, mandible, and the FIRST Neanderthal hyoid bone (matching modern speech-tract anatomy!), missing only the cranium possibly via ancient skull-removal rituals.
evidence.limits: Intentional skull retrieval vs post-burial disturbance discussed alongside KMH1 infant.

evidence.title: Amud Cave (Wadi Amud, Galilee, Israel): ~68–53 ka tallest Neanderthal (Amud 1) & infant burial
evidence.dateBasis: TL burnt-flint & ESR (Valladas et al. 1999 JAS)
evidence.summary: Amud 1 adult male burial (~1.78 m tall with largest known hominin cranial capacity ~1,740 cc!) plus Amud 7 10-month-old infant burial accompanied by a red-deer maxilla grave offering.
evidence.limits: Short, intense late Mousterian occupation dated cleanly ~55–68 ka.

evidence.title: 'Ein Qashish (Qishon Valley, Galilee, Israel): ~70–60 ka FIRST open-air Levantine Neanderthal
evidence.dateBasis: OSL fluvial dating (Been et al. 2017 Sci. Rep.; Ekshtain 2019 PLOS ONE)
evidence.summary: Lower limb bones (EQH2 femur/tibia/patella) and adult molar (EQH1) discovered in open-air floodplain mudstones (~70–60 ka), dismantling the myth that Levantine Neanderthals only used caves.
evidence.limits: Fluvial floodplain exposure preserves postcrania without cranium.

evidence.title: Shukbah Cave (Wadi en-Natuf, West Bank/Palestine): ~60–48 ka southernmost Neanderthal
evidence.dateBasis: Dorothy Garrod 1928 find & Blinkhorn/Zanolli (2021 Sci. Rep.)
evidence.summary: Micro-CT restudy by Blinkhorn & Zanolli (2021) verified Garrod's large Shukbah D molar (~7–12 yr child) as diagnostic Neanderthal paired with 'Nubian Levallois' stone points—extending confirmed Neanderthals to their southernmost point on Earth!
evidence.limits: 1928 breccia pit context lacks direct modern radiometric sample.

evidence.title: Geula Cave (Haifa, Mount Carmel, Israel): ~45–42 ka postcranial fragments
evidence.dateBasis: Late Mousterian Carmel biochronology
evidence.summary: Ulnar/humeral/cranial fragments in final Carmel Mousterian layers beside Tabun and Kebara.
evidence.limits: Minimal isolated bone fragments.

evidence.title: Dederiyeh Cave (Afrin Valley, NW Syria): ~70–50 ka Dederiyeh 1 & 2 infant burials
evidence.dateBasis: ESR & Levantine Mousterian stratigraphy (Akazawa et al. 1993)
evidence.summary: Two remarkably complete (~2-year-old) infant Neanderthal skeletons excavated in deliberate burial pits (Dederiyeh 1 extended on its back with a limestone slab beneath its head and a flint point over its heart!).
evidence.limits: Northern Levantine karst bridge between Israel/Lebanon and Caucasus/Zagros.

evidence.title: Shanidar Cave (Bradost Mountain, Iraqi Kurdistan): 75–45 ka Shanidar 1–10 & 'Shanidar Z'
evidence.dateBasis: OSL, 14C & Pomeroy et al. (2020 Antiquity; 2025) renewed excavations
evidence.summary: Ten classic skeletons (1953–60 Ralph Solecki: 'Nandy' Shanidar 1 blind/amputee elder cared for years, Shanidar 3 rib spear wound, Shanidar 4 'flower burial' cluster) joined by 2018–2025 discovery of 'Shanidar Z' articulated upper female skeleton resting directly atop pollen-clump soils!
evidence.limits: Renewed sedimentology tests insect/burrowing vs intentional wildflower placement for Shanidar 4 pollen.

evidence.title: Bisitun Cave (Kermanshah, Western Iran): ~70–45 ka Neanderthal radius & incisor
evidence.dateBasis: Trinkaus & Biglari (2006 Paléorient)
evidence.summary: Cranial incisor and proximal right radius shaft (Carleton Coon 1949), re-established in 2006 as the first morphologically confirmed Neanderthal skeletal remains inside Iran along the High Zagros pass.
evidence.limits: 1949 trench excavation lacks fine modern radiometric age control.

evidence.title: Wezmeh Cave (Islamabad-e Gharb, Kermanshah, Iran): 70–40 ka Wezmeh 1 child premolar
evidence.dateBasis: Micro-CT enamel morphometrics & U-series (Zanolli et al. 2019 JHE)
evidence.summary: Unerupted maxillary right fourth premolar (Wezmeh 1) definitively verified by 3D enamel-dentine junction imaging (2019) as a 6–10-year-old Zagros Neanderthal child—earlier misattributed to H. sapiens.
evidence.limits: Hyena-accumulated carnivore den context.

evidence.title: Bawa Yawan Rockshelter (Nawdarwan Valley, Kermanshah, Iran): 44–41 ka in situ tooth
evidence.dateBasis: Direct TL/OSL & Bayesian 14C (Heydari-Guran 2021 PLOS ONE; 2024)
evidence.summary: Left lower deciduous canine sealed in situ inside Zagros Mousterian levels dated ~43.6–41.5 ka cal BP just beneath early Baradostian/Upper Paleolithic layers—first stratified in situ Iranian Neanderthal fossil!
evidence.limits: Single pediatric canine directly below UP transition.

evidence.title: Teshik-Tash Grotto (Baisun Range, Uzbekistan): ~70–50 ka child burial & ibex horns
evidence.dateBasis: Krause et al. (2007 Nature) mtDNA & Central Asian Mousterian context
evidence.summary: Excavated in 1938: ~9-year-old child cranium and skeleton buried amid five ringed pairs of Siberian mountain-goat (ibex) horns; 2007 mtDNA confirmed Teshik-Tash belongs closely to European rather than archaic Asian clades—marking a massive steppe migration!
evidence.limits: Modern direct collagen date remains elusive; ring of horns debated between ritual burial and cave-wall taphonomy.

evidence.title: Obi-Rakhmat Grotto (Paltau Valley, Tashkent, Uzbekistan): 90–60 ka OR-1 mosaic child
evidence.dateBasis: U-series, ESR & Glantz et al. (2008 JHE) / Krivoshapkin (2010)
evidence.summary: Over 150 cranial fragments and six maxillary teeth (OR-1, ~9–12-year-old child) pairing classic Neanderthal huge dentition with atypically thin, high/globular parietal vaults along the Tian Shan foothills—possibly reflecting population contact or eastern peripheral drift.
evidence.limits: No nuclear DNA extracted yet from OR-1 to distinguish archaic drift from introgression.

evidence.title: Anghilak Cave (Kashkadarya, Zarafshan Range, Uzbekistan): ~45–30 ka metatarsal
evidence.dateBasis: AMS 14C & Glantz et al. (2008 JHE / Antiquity)
evidence.summary: Isolated large fifth metatarsal (AH-1) demonstrating robust Neanderthal-like forefoot mechanics in southern Uzbekistan between Teshik-Tash and Samarkand.
evidence.limits: Single isolated foot bone inside multi-horizon cave.

evidence.title: Denisova Cave East Chamber (Altai, Siberia): ~120 ka Denisova 5 'Altai Neanderthal' genome
evidence.dateBasis: OSL, U-Th & Prüfer/Massilani (2014–2026) high-coverage nuclear genome
evidence.summary: Adult female pedal phalanx (Denisova 5, East Chamber Layer 11.4, ~120 ka) delivering the foundational high-coverage 'Altai Neanderthal' nuclear genome revealing high inbreeding (half-sibling parents) and representing the FIRST eastward Neanderthal wave across Eurasia before Denisovans & later 60 ka Micoquian Neanderthals.
evidence.limits: Co-occupied the same cave system intermittently with Denisovans across ~200 kyr.

evidence.title: Okladnikov Cave (Sibiryachikha, Altai, Siberia): ~47–40 ka EASTERNMOST Neanderthals
evidence.dateBasis: Krause et al. (2007 Nature) mtDNA, Kolobova (2020) & Skov/Massilani (2022–2026)
evidence.summary: Humeri, juvenile femur, and teeth associated with Sibiryachikha/Micoquian tools representing the EASTERNMOST confirmed Neanderthal skeletal fossils known on Earth (~51.7°N, 84°E)—genetically tied to the second ~60–50 ka Eastern European dispersal alongside Chagyrskaya.
evidence.limits: Subadult fragmentary limbs alongside fauna; sits ~100 km northwest of Denisova Cave.

waves.title: Early Neanderthal Lineage Divergence & Accretion Across Western Eurasia
waves.summary: Sima de los Huesos (Atapuerca, 430 ka nuclear DNA), Swanscombe (~400 ka), and Qaleh Kurd (~450–150 ka) demonstrate early Neanderthal genetic and cranial emergence well before classic MIS 5e/4 forms.
waves.limits: Mid-Pleistocene fossil sparsity masks finer regional boundaries between H. heidelbergensis and proto-Neanderthals.

waves.title: Last Interglacial (MIS 5e) Northern & Mediterranean Expansion
waves.summary: Temperate MIS 5e broadleaf woodland expansion carried genetically continuous Neanderthal groups across Scladina, Hohlenstein-Stadel, Krapina, and Poland north of the Carpathians.
waves.limits: MIS 5e forest density challenged terrestrial megafauna ambush but left abundant travertine and karst sites.

waves.title: Levant–Anatolia–Zagros Coastal & Highland Refugia Corridor
waves.summary: Mediterranean coastal plains and Taurus–Zagros valleys sustained Tabun, Kebara, Amud, Ein Qashish, Shukbah, Dederiyeh, Shanidar, Bisitun, Wezmeh, and Bawa Yawan across glacial shifts.
waves.limits: Exact southward push into Sinai vs local MIS 5–3 coexistence with early H. sapiens remains actively modeled.

waves.title: First Eastward Neanderthal Dispersal to Altai Siberia (Denisova 5)
waves.summary: MIS 5e/5 warming corridors across southern Russia or Iran/Central Asia brought deeply inbred Altai Neanderthals (Denisova 5) ~4,000 km eastward into southern Siberia.
waves.limits: Vast Kazakh/Turanian steppe gap yields sparse skeletal fossils between Uzbekistan and Altai.

waves.title: Second Eastward Micoquian Dispersal (Crimea/Caucasus → Chagyrskaya & Okladnikov)
waves.summary: Backed by 2020/2025 archaeological and aDNA evidence (Chagyrskaya, Okladnikov, and Starosele 2025 PNAS), Micoquian bison-hunting Neanderthals swept thousands of kilometers east from Crimea/North Caucasus/Eastern Europe across Eurasian steppes.
waves.limits: Genetic turnover replaced earlier Altai Neanderthals near 60 ka before total extinction ~42–40 ka.

waves.title: Late Extinction Window & Fragmented Refugia (Iberia, Rhône, Belgium, Crimea)
waves.summary: Small isolated metapopulations (Mandrin 'Thorin', El Sidrón, Spy/Goyet, Feldhofer, Vindija, Subalyuk, Sima de las Palomas, Gorham's) disappeared mosaic-by-mosaic across Europe by ~40–39 ka.
waves.limits: Genetic isolation ('Thorin' 50 kyr split) indicates demographic fragility compounded by rapid climate swings and H. sapiens arrivals.

waves.title: Neanderthal–Denisovan & Neanderthal–Homo sapiens Interbreeding Horizon
waves.summary: Direct genetic proof of cross-lineage families: Denisova 11 ('Denny', F1 Neanderthal mother + Denisovan father ~90 ka), Levantine/Zagros pulse (~60–50 ka contributing ~2% ancestry to non-Africans), and Peștera cu Oase 1 (~40 ka H. sapiens with a Neanderthal ancestor 4–6 generations earlier).
waves.limits: Schematic genetic interaction links across Southwest Asia, Danube, and Altai crossroads.

studies.title: Homo neanderthalensis: Comprehensive Eurasian Fossil & aDNA Atlas (~430–37 ka)
studies.summary: Playable Eurasian fossil atlas uniting 121 confirmed Neanderthal skeletal, dental, and ancient-DNA localities from Portugal, Gibraltar, Wales, and Doggerland across France, Italy, Central/East Europe, Crimea, Caucasus, Levant, and Zagros to Teshik-Tash, Chagyrskaya, and Okladnikov in Siberia.
